summary.headline: IGL Q1 FY27 PAT of INR186 crore and EBITDA of INR296 crore, with turnover a record INR5,028 crore despite costlier West Asia-linked gas.
summary.overview: Indraprastha Gas reported record quarterly turnover of INR5,028 crore (about 16% up YoY), EBITDA of INR296 crore and PAT of INR186 crore, with profitability hit by higher gas costs from the West Asia disruption. Average daily gas sales rose to 9.66 MMSCMD from 9.13 MMSCMD, and CNG volumes grew about 6% overall (about 11% excluding DTC and DIMTS, 9% in Delhi, 27% in new GAs outside Delhi). Management said long-term EBITDA guidance of about INR7/SCM is unchanged, but it declined to give a near-term margin view. Q1 capex was INR327 crore. This was the first call for new MD Kumar Shanker and CFO Manjeet Gulati.

segments.name: CNG (overall)
segments.commentary: Overall CNG volume up about 6% YoY; about 11% excluding DTC and DIMTS; Delhi up about 9% excluding DTC. Peak single-day sales reached 58 lakh kg. DTC volume is now effectively zero versus 1.5 lakh kg/day a year earlier; DIMTS holds around 1.5 lakh kg/day.

segments.name: New GAs outside Delhi NCR
segments.commentary: CNG volumes grew about 27% YoY; management said about 50% of incremental sales came from new GAs.

segments.name: CUGL
segments.commentary: Total volume rose from 0.34 to 0.36 MMSCMD (about 6%); CNG 0.23 to 0.25 MMSCMD (about 8%); PNG flat at about 0.11-0.12 MMSCMD.

segments.name: MNGL
segments.commentary: Total volume rose 18% from 1.85 to 2.19 MMSCMD; CNG 1.27 to 1.44 MMSCMD (about 13%); PNG 0.58 to 0.75 MMSCMD (about 29%), helped by direct Samruddhi pipeline supply to Nashik.

guidance_outlook: Long-term EBITDA guidance of about INR7 per SCM is maintained, but management said near-term margins will be difficult to call given geopolitics; it declined to comment on the quarter.
Capex plan: about INR1,800-2,000 crore overall, with INR1,200-1,500 crore on core business and INR500-600 crore possible from new business development and diversification.
Management expects CNG demand to grow faster after GST 2.0 cuts, citing about 27,300 vehicle additions/conversions per month over the last 6 months versus 18,000 a year earlier.
Delhi EV mandate (from 1 Jan 2027) is expected to reduce CNG volumes by less than 1% in 2027 and 2-3% by 2030.
Hedging via Henry Hub-linked instruments started in May 2026 and will continue.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex was INR327 crore.
Steel network expanded about 25 km to about 2,600 km; MDPE pipeline added about 500 km in the quarter.
Commissioned a new city gate station at Rohini, Delhi.
Commenced LNG operations in NCR with CONCOR, the first in the NCR region.
Commissioned a CNG station with PNG at the Noida International Airport; added about 1 lakh-plus PNG and about 530 industrial and commercial connections in the quarter.
demand_pricing: Gas sourcing is about 48% domestic (APM, New Well Gas and HPHT) and about 52% imported, on about 9.5 MMSCMD sold. Imported volume is about 4-4.1 MMSCMD, of which about 3.9-4.0 MMSCMD is long-term contracts, 0.6-0.7 MMSCMD pool gas, and 0.25-0.3 MMSCMD spot.
Spot LNG ranged from about USD17-18 to USD21-22/MMBtu during the quarter.
New Well Gas fell below 1 MMSCMD from about 1.26 MMSCMD previously; HPHT was 0.6-0.7 MMSCMD and is expected to rise with contract closures in September.
Delhi vehicle mix of CNG sales: passenger cars about 48-50%, commercial vehicles about 19%, taxis about 14%, buses about 12%, and 3-wheeler autos about 7-8%, mostly Delhi.
CNG share of Delhi/NCR vehicle population is about 24-25%; about 42% of new passenger vehicle registrations in Delhi are CNG.
Management sees a fuel-price advantage over petrol of about INR17 per unit and wants to use it to grow volumes.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sourcing mix between APM, HPHT, New Well Gas and long-term versus spot LNG?
qa_highlights.answer: About 48% domestic and 52% imported; imported is about 3.9-4.0 MMSCMD long-term, 0.6-0.7 MMSCMD pool gas and 0.25-0.3 MMSCMD spot. Management aims to raise HPHT share.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook for the next 6-9 months?
qa_highlights.answer: Long-term EBITDA guidance of about INR7/SCM stays, but subsequent quarters will be hard to judge. Management cited four factors: US supply, Middle East geopolitics, China/Japan demand, and European storage and the winter outlook.

qa_highlights.question: Will CNG growth reach double digits?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, pointing to about 4.6 lakh passenger vehicles added in July 2026 and Maruti's 42% CNG share. Outside-Delhi GAs grew about 27%, and Delhi about 9-10% excluding DTC.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the Delhi EV policy on volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Less than 1% CNG volume impact in 2027 and about 2-3% by 2030; the policy applies to Delhi only, not Noida or Gurugram.

qa_highlights.question: Is hedging being used to reduce spot LNG exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Hedging via Henry Hub-linked instruments started in May 2026 and is seen as an important tool.

qa_highlights.question: Gas cost per SCM and July trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 gas cost was about INR40-45/SCM; management declined to give July detail, saying prices had risen again.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a GST move on natural gas?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the decision rests with the GST Council and there is no evidence of a major change yet.

risks_watch: Spot LNG price volatility and force majeure cuts from West Asia; spot was about 3% of sourcing.
EBITDA margin recovery toward INR7/SCM is uncertain; gas costs were about INR40-45/SCM in Q1 and rose again in July.
Delhi policy: no new 3-wheeler registrations and commercial vehicle registrations from 1 Jan 2027; school buses must switch 30% by 2030.
Gurugram and Faridabad authorisation remains in litigation; only part of Gurugram services have started.
CUGL volume growth remains slow (about 0.36 MMSCMD), attributed to price sensitivity and the tax structure in its C&I segment.
Domestic supply mix shifts (New Well Gas decline) and HPHT contract renewals due around September.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volumes and CNG demand growth, but cautious and often non-committal on near-term margins and gas costs, which management said are unpredictable. It repeatedly declined to give quarter-level EBITDA or July gas price detail and described the outlook as "very, very highly unpredictable".
key_quotes: So, in fact, you'll be glad to know that in recent days, we have touched the peak sale of up to even 58 lakhs kg in a single day, which is not only among the highest for IGL in its history, but also definitely the highest in the country for any CGD company in the country.
So, long term, yes, spot will be there a little bit. But I think if we are able to get the gas from our long-term contracts, our aspiration, our vision is that.

So, overall, we have evaluated the scenario of the sales volume being lost vis-a-vis being added through the natural growth in particularly with a very, very strong segment from the passenger car vehicles, the expected growth is coming.
But in such an unpredictable and volatile situation of the geopolitics, it will be very, very difficult to comment for the quarter.

CNG station with PNG at Noida International Airport

growth.why: Management held long-term EBITDA guidance of about INR7/SCM and total FY27 capex of INR1,800-2,000 crore (core INR1,200-1,500 crore), but declined to give a near-term margin view; growth is supported by new GA CNG volumes (+27%), CNG vehicle additions of 27,300/month vs 18,000, and recently commissioned stations and pipeline, with no quantified volume target for FY27.

mgmt.note: New MD Kumar Shanker and CFO Manjeet Gulati held their first call in Q1 FY27, signalling volume growth via the fuel-price advantage and diversification capex, though no specific targets were given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management declined to give a near-term margin view; Q1 gas cost was about INR40-45/SCM, prices rose again in July, and EBITDA recovery to INR7/SCM long-term guidance is uncertain.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: FY27 capex plan of INR1,800-2,000 crore total (core INR1,200-1,500 crore) was held, with steel network at about 2,600 km and about 500 km of MDPE added in Q1, so further pipeline and station build-out is guided.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Average daily gas sales rose to 9.66 MMSCMD from 9.13 (about +6%), new GAs' CNG volumes grew about 27%, and vehicle additions/conversions were about 27,300 per month versus 18,000 a year earlier.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is already guided at INR1,800-2,000 crore for FY27 and Q1 spend was INR327 crore; utilisation was not disclosed, so no new capex programme is signalled beyond the existing plan.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Long-term EBITDA guidance of about INR7/SCM was only held, and management declined to comment on near-term margins amid volatile spot LNG (USD17-22/MMBtu).

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Gas costs of INR40-45/SCM in Q1 rose again in July, HPHT contract renewals are due around September, and New Well Gas fell below 1 MMSCMD from about 1.26 MMSCMD.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product, brand or model launches were discussed; the call covered commissioned stations, pipelines and LNG operations only.

rows.label: Fuel-price advantage over petrol used to grow CNG volumes
rows.why: Management sees a fuel-price advantage of about INR17 per unit over petrol and plans to use it to grow volumes, with CNG growth expected to be double-digit after GST 2.0 cuts.

rows.label: Delhi EV mandate from 1 Jan 2027
rows.why: Management expects the mandate to cut CNG volumes by less than 1% in 2027 and 2-3% by 2030, so the impact on the window is small.

rows.label: Henry Hub-linked hedging to reduce spot LNG exposure
rows.why: Hedging started in May 2026 and will continue, though spot LNG was only about 0.25-0.3 MMSCMD (about 3% of sourcing), so the effect on margins is limited.

tone.note: Management was confident on CNG volume growth (new GAs +27%, Delhi +9% ex-DTC) but cautious and non-committal on near-term margins and gas costs, repeatedly declining to give quarter-level EBITDA or July gas prices; analysts pushed on margin outlook and gas sourcing.

quality.why: Turnover grew about 16% YoY with average daily gas sales up from 9.13 to 9.66 MMSCMD (about 6%), with CNG growth broad-based (about 11% excluding DTC and DIMTS, 27% in new GAs outside Delhi); the brief cites no one-off gains or low-base effects, and the gap between turnover and volume growth looks like gas price pass-through, though the brief does not state this explicitly.
